proposal.title: Credit-spread-wide book: cap the small-value sleeve and extend the trend overlay to IWN
proposal.rationale: The implemented credit-spread-wide book holds IWN at 40%, but the source corpus's slowdown portfolio (Dow Jones IG 50% / 10Y Treasuries 40% / small value 10%) caps small value at 10% — the implementation quadruples the equity beta of the most defensive book in the stack. The 200d trend overlay is applied only to SPY and GLD, leaving IWN unprotected even though it is the equity sleeve most sensitive to credit conditions: today IWN's tape (speed -55, accel -73) is worse than SPY's, and the stack's -13.3% max drawdown — worst in the ranked table — is the measurable fingerprint of that concentration. Proposed revision: (a) in the credit-spread-wide book, cap IWN at 15% and move the residual to IEF/TLT; (b) apply the same 200d trend overlay to IWN that SPY receives, redirecting to the haven when below trend. This is a claim about the RULE, not this month's reading, and should be measured in probation rather than applied on conviction.

spec.current_rule: credit-spread-wide book = {IEF: 50, IWN: 40, GLD: 10}; 200d trend overlay on SPY and GLD only
spec.proposed_rule: credit-spread-wide book = {IEF: 50, IEF/TLT: 35, IWN: 15, GLD: 10} (weights normalized to 100); extend the 200d trend overlay to IWN, redirecting to the haven sleeve when IWN is below its 200d MA
spec.evidence: source passage: slowdown portfolio = 50% IG bonds / 40% 10Y / 10% small value; ms-stack maxDD -13.3% vs defender -4.4%; IWN speed -54.7, accel -73.1 at decision date 2008-07-01

scenarios.bull: spread mean-reverts below median quickly; small-value cap forfeits some rebound upside — bounded cost
scenarios.base: spread wide 2-3 quarters; reduced equity beta cuts drawdown, overlay catches further deterioration
scenarios.bear: spread blows out past 4.0 (corpus threshold where equities underperform cash); capped, overlaid IWN is the difference between a -5% and a -15% event

proposal.title: Extend the 200d trend overlay to all risky-equity sleeves (IWN), not only SPY
proposal.rationale: In the credit-spread-wide book the stack currently holds IWN 40% while the premise of that book is impaired credit. The 200-day overlay redirects the SPY sleeve to the haven but never examines IWN, so the stack can be 40% long the most credit-sensitive equity class precisely when its own signal says credit is broken. This month is the live example: book = credit-spread-wide (BAA10Y 3.22 vs median 2.29), SPY overlay active, yet IWN 40% rides on momentum (speed +44) that the rule never checks against its own trend. The fix is mechanical and testable: apply the same 200-day-MA redirect to every risky-equity sleeve in every book, redirecting to the same haven sleeve. Over 1991-present this would have mattered most in 2000-02 and 2008-09, exactly the windows the stack is designed for. Let it earn or lose FAVORS in probation rather than be applied on one cycle's conviction.

spec.current_rule: 200-day trend overlay applied to SPY (and GLD) sleeves only; other equity sleeves in a decided book are taken as-is
spec.proposed_rule: Apply the 200-day trend overlay to every risky-equity sleeve in every book (SPY, IWN, EFA and any future equity sleeve): sleeve below its own 200d MA -> redirect that sleeve's weight to the book's haven sleeve; sleeve above -> hold
spec.evidence: 2008-08-01 cycle: book credit-spread-wide, BAA10Y 3.22 vs 2.29 median, SPY below trend and redirected, but IWN 40% unexamined; small-cap value is the equity class most exposed to a widening BAA spread via the refinancing channel
spec.expected_effect: Reduced max drawdown in credit-spread-wide regimes at the cost of occasional whipsaw on small-cap momentum; measurable against the existing stack in replay

proposal.title: Market-signal stack: regime-conditioned inflation-hedge floor before trend redirect
proposal.rationale: This month the credit-spread-wide book plus 200d overlay moved from {IEF 50, IWN 40, GLD 10} to {IEF 60, IWN 40} — mechanically correct given gold is below its 200d line (speed -295, accelerating down), but it leaves the adopted allocation with zero inflation hedge in a regime detected as stagflation (falling growth, CPI 5.4% and rising, negative real rates). The active invariant complex contradicts a fully nominal book here: 01KY2N410K3N39TB6T6C1721MW (weight 0.80: negative real rates shift investors to inflation-hedge assets, which outperform nominal bonds), inv-inflation-persistence-tips (0.61), and 01KY2MW85Q6JHMNRVPAHMJNQTC (>5% inflation: gold and commodities outperform the median asset class). The trend overlay was validated as a drawdown cap on the book as a whole; it was not confronted on the specific question of whether the inflation-hedge sleeve should be trend-exempt when the macro regime is stagflationary. 2008 is precisely the case to test: if the growth collapse resolves as deflationary recession, the redirect is right; if inflation persists above 5% while real rates stay negative, the redirect removes the only sleeve that hedges the regime. This is a rule-level disagreement, so it should be measured in probation, not applied once.

spec.current_rule: 200d trend overlay redirects any sleeve below its 200d moving average to the haven asset, unconditionally
spec.proposed_revision: When the contemporaneous regime is falling-growth-rising-inflation (or CPI > 5% with negative real short rates), retain a minimum inflation-hedge floor (e.g. 10% gold or TIPS) in the selected book before applying the trend overlay; the overlay continues to apply to all equity sleeves and to any hedge allocation above the floor
spec.test_evidence: Regime detector stagflation confidence 86.9 on 2008-09; BAA10Y 3.29 vs 2.3 median; gold redirect removed the last hedge sleeve on 2008-09-02
spec.backtest_expectation: Compare current rule vs floored variant over stagflation windows (1973-74, 1979-80, 2007-08H2, 2022): accept if floored variant improves Sortino/Calmar in-regime without degrading out-of-regime drawdown control beyond a configured tolerance

proposal.title: Extend the market-signal 200d trend overlay to the equity sleeve of the credit-spread-wide book (IWN)
proposal.rationale: On 2008-10-01 the overlay redirected SPY and GLD (both below their 200d trend) to the haven, but the credit-spread-wide book's 40% IWN sleeve carries no trend check. IWN is in an accelerating crash — speed -33.2, acceleration -57.6, WORSE acceleration than the SPY sleeve the overlay did protect (-186 vs -58 on acceleration is worse for SPY, but IWN's acceleration is deteriorating faster relative to its own recent history and its speed is unambiguously negative) — and small-cap value in a credit crisis is financials-heavy, the epicenter exposure (invariant 01KY2NVPNGBF5CJ7NS93Y2842R). The instrument therefore holds 40% in an unprotected risk asset precisely when its own overlay logic says risk assets below trend should be redirected. This is a rule-level gap, not a one-month reading: any credit-spread-wide episode with falling equities will reproduce it. Applying the same 200d trend test to the book's equity sleeve (whatever ticker it holds) and redirecting to the haven when below trend is a small, symmetric extension of an already-validated rule. Filed as a revision so it earns adoption through probation and FAVORS measurement rather than being applied once on conviction; the stack's own stagflation FAVORS (maxDD -2.8% over 11 periods vs the live book's -13.3% this cycle) suggest the measured version of the rule already implies tighter drawdown control than the current overlay coverage delivers.

spec.current_rule: 200d trend overlay applied to SPY and GLD only; other sleeves (e.g., IWN in the credit-spread-wide book) held regardless of trend
spec.proposed_rule: Apply the 200d trend overlay to every risk-asset sleeve of the selected book, including the small-cap value sleeve (IWN); redirect below-trend sleeves to the haven exactly as SPY/GLD are today
spec.evidence: 2008-10-01: IWN speed -33.19, acceleration -57.56 while held at 40% with no overlay; SPY/GLD redirected the same day; live book maxDD -13.3% vs strategy FAVORS stagflation maxDD -2.8%
spec.hypothesis: Overlay-complete books show smaller crisis-window drawdowns than overlay-partial books without giving up the spread signal's regime-selection edge

proposal.title: Market-signal stack: add a spread-rate-of-change (wideningspeed) guard to the book-selection rule
proposal.rationale: The rule selects its book on BAA10Y LEVEL vs its 10y median (2.27 vs 2.59 = tight) and applies a 200d trend overlay only to the sleeves, not to the signal itself. In February 2020 the spread was tight-but-gap-widening while VIX went 15 -> 40 in two weeks; the level-vs-median test cannot distinguish a stable tight spread from one mid-dislocation, so the stack sat 50% in SPY through the fastest correction in decades. A widening-speed guard (e.g., if BAA10Y 1-month change exceeds its own 90th percentile historically, defer to the defensive book or force the trend overlay to a shorter window) would have caught 2008, 2011, 2015-16 and 2020 spread regimes earlier. This is a claim about the RULE, not this month's reading, so it belongs in probation where FAVORS can measure it, not in the assessment field.

spec.current_rule: book = f(BAA10Y level vs 10y trailing median, T10Y2Y level vs 10y trailing median); 200d trend overlay on sleeves
spec.proposed_rule: add guard: if BAA10Y 1-month change > 90th percentile of its trailing 10y changes, override to the most defensive book (or halve equity sleeve) until spread speed normalizes for 2 consecutive monthly prints
spec.evidence: 2020-02: BAA10Y 2.27 (tight vs median) while VIX 15->40 and SPY acceleration -239; analogous rapid-widening episodes 2008, 2011, 2015-16 in the 35-year backtest window
spec.scope: paper-mode probation; measure hit rate and turnover cost against the unmodified rule

proposal.title: Audit the market-signal stack backtest-to-live drawdown divergence
proposal.rationale: The stack's confronted FAVORS record in falling-growth-falling-inflation shows maxDD -4.7% and calmar 5.05 over n=15, yet the live paper portfolio (ms-stack) has already realized -23.8% maxDD and calmar 0.155 since adoption — a 5x divergence on the risk metric the owner actually experiences. Either the backtest understates the concentrated books' path risk (sleeve construction, monthly decision cadence, trend-overlay lag in fast crashes like March 2020), or the FAVORS window is unrepresentative. If the confronted numbers are overstating the live risk envelope, every downstream consumer of those FAVORS rows — verdicts, ranking commentary, probation decisions — is leaning on a flattering mirror. This should be measured, not argued.

spec.audit_scope: ms-stack live NAV path vs backtested path for identical signal decisions since adoption
questions: Does the backtest apply the 200d trend overlay with the same knowable-at-date discipline as live?
Does the monthly decision cadence in the backtest match live, or does the backtest rebalance on information not knowable at decision time?
Is the March 2020 crash path present in the confronted FAVORS window, and if so why does its maxDD bound at -4.7% when the live book lost -23.8%?
Should FAVORS rows for the concentrated books carry a path-risk haircut until live and backtest reconcile?
spec.deliverable: reconciliation report; if divergence is methodological, a corrected backtest trace; if genuine, a data-quality flag on the stack's FAVORS rows

proposal.title: Inflation gate for the market-signal book (CPI >= 5% shifts 10 pts SPY -> GLD)
proposal.rationale: The market-signal rule reads two coincident prices (credit spread, yield slope) and one trend. In an inflation shock, spreads stay tight precisely until policy stress reaches credit — the signal is late by construction. The 2022-01-03 entry demonstrates the gap: 60% equity into CPI 5.1% with liquidity speed -0.69 and a 70.6-confidence stagflation call from the regime engine. The corpus already holds this knowledge (inv-high-inflation-equities, integrated, market_score 0.67; the >5% returns-cliff invariant; inv-inflation-persistence-tips 0.82) — the instrument just has no input to express it. A 10-pt SPY->GLD gate when trailing CPI YoY >= 5% keeps the rule's anti-drift value while removing its largest blind spot. Proposed for probation: measured monthly against the unmodified stack, adopted or closed mechanically on FAVORS — proven, not applied on conviction.

spec.measurement: Paper-mode the gated variant against the unmodified stack over the same monthly decision dates; compare sortino/calmar/maxDD in falling-growth-rising-inflation and rising-growth-rising-inflation regimes; adopt or close mechanically on FAVORS after probation.
spec.rule_current: Book selection keys only on BAA10Y vs its 10y trailing median and T10Y2Y vs its 10y trailing median; the credit-spread-tight-yield-curve-flat book is fixed at SPY 50 / GLD 40 / IWN 10 with a 200d trend overlay per sleeve.
spec.rule_proposed: Add an inflation gate at the decision date: when trailing CPI YoY >= 5.0, shift 10 points from SPY to GLD within the credit-spread-tight-yield-curve-flat book (50/40/10 -> 40/50/10); unchanged otherwise. 200d trend overlay and binding caps still apply on top.
spec.trigger_evidence: 2022-01-03 opening entry: 60% equity (SPY 50 + IWN 10) with CPI YoY 5.1, growth composite 100.5 falling (speed -1.22, accel -0.72), global liquidity speed -0.69, regime stagflation conf 70.6. BAA10Y 1.85 vs median 2.39 is tight because policy stress has not yet reached credit — both signal inputs are coincident, not leading, for an inflation shock.

proposal.title: Trend-overlay haven redirect should be regime- and trend-aware (not always IEF)
proposal.rationale: The market-signal stack's 200d overlay correctly exits GLD when below trend (per invariant 01KY2QBRQJ6BSS25TA6DGSW98V: below-MA gold ~0.0% returns), but it redirects the sleeve to IEF unconditionally. In a negative-real-yield, rising-inflation, tightening-liquidity regime, IEF is not a haven — it is the asset the regime punishes most (inv-low-real-rate-nominal-bonds, ACTIVE; inv-inflation-persistence-tips, ACTIVE). February 2022 is the live case: GLD below trend triggers the redirect while IEF itself is in a downtrend (speed -12.1, acceleration -8.2) with CPI 5.1% and global liquidity speed -0.248. The overlay vets the trend of what it sells but not of what it buys, and it never asks whether duration is a haven in THIS regime. A rule measured over 35 years that contains an unconditional assumption is exactly the kind of thing a probation slot exists to test.

spec.revision: When the GLD sleeve fails its 200d trend check, redirect to the haven ONLY if the haven itself passes (a) its own 200d trend check and (b) a real-yield/regime gate (e.g., redirect to IEF only when not in falling-growth-rising-inflation or when 10y real yield > 0); otherwise redirect to the shortest-duration haven (SHY or cash). Symmetrically, consider applying the same veto to any automatic haven leg.
spec.current_behavior: GLD below 200d MA -> sleeve redirected to IEF unconditionally.
spec.evidence: 2022-02-01 decision: GLD->IEF redirect while IEF speed -12.1/accel -8.2, inflation 5.1%, real yields negative, liquidity speed -0.248; ms-stack live maxDD -23.8%, calmar 0.515, worst on the board; stack FAVORS in falling-growth-rising-inflation (sortino 1.80) is its weakest quadrant.

proposal.title: Inflation-aware duration substitution in the market-signal defensive books
proposal.rationale: The tight-spread/flat-curve book in force holds 50% IEF — nominal intermediate duration — while CPI runs 8.7% and rising with deeply negative real rates. The signal reads two prices and one trend; it cannot see that the 'defensive' asset its defensive books lean on is the one the inflation regime punishes. The live record corroborates: ms-stack 1y -11.2%, maxDD -23.8%, worst Calmar on the roster. The two probation revisions already pending address the haven redirect and a SPY->GLD gate, but neither touches the duration composition of the defensive books themselves — the gate as proposed shifts SPY->GLD and would not even bind this month (the book holds no SPY). This revision targets the actual blind spot and gets measured over probation instead of overriding the book once on conviction.

spec.current_behavior: Tight-spread books (slowdown/countercyclical) allocate their defensive sleeve to nominal intermediate/long duration (IEF/TLT-class) regardless of the inflation level; trend overlay redirects equity sleeves to a fixed haven.
spec.proposed_revision: When CPI YoY >= 5% at the monthly decision date, substitute up to half of the nominal-duration sleeve of tight-spread defensive books with TIP and/or SHY (short real/nominal duration); revert when CPI YoY falls below 4% or real 10y yields turn positive. Thresholds to be tuned in backtest over 1991-present, explicitly including 2022.

Precedent concern: 2022 is the first post-1991 episode combining tight spreads with >8% inflation, so backtest must confirm the substitution does not degrade the 1994/2000/2008/2020 readings
spec.expected_effect: Reduce drawdown and improve Calmar of the tight-spread defensive books in high-inflation tightening episodes without altering the spread/slope book-selection rule itself.
spec.risk: If the 2022 window is sui generis, the overlay adds turnover for little gain; probation measurement settles this.
